title: Running the School
answer: Part IV, Running the School, covers teacher planning and grading, assessment and data, operations and finance, and people and leadership. These chapters speak most directly to principals, district leaders, and board members.

children.name: Teacher Planning, Grading, and Feedback
children.blurb: Fifteen teachers in five primary schools in England used AI to help plan lessons for two school terms. Their self reported weekly planning time fell by 52.5 percent, from about 10 hours to under 5 (Carson et al., 2026).

children.name: Assessment, Data, and the Early Warning System
children.blurb: Researchers who build systems to predict student failure found something troubling when they looked closely. A single accuracy number made predictions look more reliable than they were.

children.name: Operations, Facilities, Transportation, and Finance
children.blurb: Boston Public Schools once faced a transportation problem that cost more than $100 million a year. Researchers built an optimization system that redesigned the bus routes, saving about $5 million a year and removing 50 buses while keeping service quality (Bertsimas et al., 2019).

children.name: People, Leadership, and Culture
children.blurb: Researchers interviewed leaders in six Colorado school districts about how they first responded to AI. Some wrote informal guidelines, some banned student use, and some updated their acceptable use policies (McGuire et al., 2026).

sections.body: This part of school life is the work of running a school and a district. The book groups that work into teacher planning and grading, assessment and data, operations and finance, and people and leadership. These chapters speak most directly to principals, district leaders, and board members. The book's text for this section does not name specific AI uses in these areas. The final chapter states the core argument of the Volume and offers a plan for the first 90 days, and a short conclusion looks back at what the evidence shows and ahead to what may change.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The book's text for this section does not list what works and what does not. It points instead to the final chapter, which states the core argument of the Volume in full. The rule it holds to is that core argument. The final chapter also sets out the first 90 days. The conclusion then looks back at what the evidence shows and ahead to what may change.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The four pages sit together as the last four chapters on running a school and a district. A teacher would go to Teacher Planning, Grading, and Feedback for the work of planning and grading. A leader would go to Assessment, Data, and the Early Warning System for assessment and data, to Operations, Facilities, Transportation, and Finance for operations and finance, and to People, Leadership, and Culture for people and leadership. The book says these chapters speak most directly to principals, district leaders, and board members. It does not say what a parent would go to them for.
